newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Dec retail sales fall 0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Dec retail sales fall 0.3 pct.

text.p: Canadian retail sales fell 0.3 percent in December to a seasonally adjusted C$18.45 billion from a revised C$18.51 billion (C$18.43 billion) in November, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a -0.4 +2.3 C$13.82 bln
Statistics Canada said early indications for January sales indicated a drop in new motor vehicle sales.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.7 percent rise in retail sales in December after November's 0.9 percent rise.

The federal agency said that despite the seasonally adjusted fall from November, retailers enjoyed stronger Christmas sales than the year before. Consumers spent C$37 billion seasonally adjusted in November and December, 4.5 percent more than in the last two Christmas seasons.
Growth was strongest in drug stores (+1.8 percent), clothing (+1.3 percent), food (+0.1 percent) and automotive (+0.1 percent).

Annually, retail sales grew by 2.4 percent in unadjusted data to C$216.6 billion in 1996 after a 2.3 percent rise in 1995. This was driven largely by the automotive sector, with motor vehicle and recreational vehicle dealers showing a 5.3 percent increase to C$52.2 billion.
Retail and general merchandise stores rose 5.0 percent in the year, led by discount department stores rising 8.6 percent while clothing, furniture and other retail stores fell.

For January 1997, in addition to the drop in new motor vehicles, Statscan said employment in the retail trade in January declined by 2,000. It pointed to a 7.8 percent rise in housing starts and higher retail trade in the United States.
